causal_assumptions.consistency: Test contexts instantiate the study-specific physical or virtual context manipulation.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported by randomized group assignment or counterbalanced within-participant context order.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Included participants could be observed in the relevant test-context conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Difference in conditioned responding when testing occurs outside versus inside the extinction context.

confidence.rationale: Controlled context manipulations support a narrow causal effect, with convergence across startle, skin conductance, and ratings but limited generalization beyond laboratory samples.

limitations: Context manipulations differ substantially between studies.

boundary_conditions: Effect magnitude depends on context contrast, timing, and measurement channel.
Laboratory renewal is not identical to clinical relapse.
scope.population: Healthy adults in differential aversive-conditioning experiments.
scope.temporal_scope: Immediate or delayed testing after successful within-session extinction.

claims.statement: Testing outside the extinction context can increase previously extinguished conditioned responding in human laboratory paradigms.
claims.temporal_ordering: Acquisition and extinction precede randomized or counterbalanced test-context exposure.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Delayed tests follow the study-specific protocol.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Timing and extinction conditions are experimentally assigned in the included studies.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Relevant timing conditions are represented in each experimental design.

claims.causal_estimand: Change from late extinction to delayed test in differential conditioned responding.

confidence.rationale: Human experiments demonstrate recovery after a delay, while its magnitude and sensitivity to acquisition-to-extinction timing vary.

limitations: A time contrast cannot uniquely identify decay, temporal-context change, or memory competition.

boundary_conditions: Recovery depends on procedural timing and the selected response measure.
scope.population: Healthy adults in laboratory threat-conditioning paradigms.

claims.statement: Under the tested timing arrangements, conditioned responding can recover after successful within-session extinction.
claims.temporal_ordering: Extinction response reduction precedes the delayed recovery test.

confidence.rationale: Renewal and spontaneous recovery are difficult to reconcile with complete erasure, but behavioral return-of-fear effects do not uniquely identify the internal representation or neural mechanism.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The broad account would be weakened by reliable, general, measurement-independent elimination of conditioned responding across context, time, and reinstatement tests after ordinary cue-only extinction.
limitations: Evidence is indirect with respect to latent memory contents.

boundary_conditions: Some procedures may also modify original learning.
The hypothesis does not require a single unitary inhibitory trace.
scope.population: Humans in laboratory Pavlovian threat-conditioning paradigms.

claims.statement: Extinction commonly adds context-sensitive learning that competes with conditioned responding rather than completely erasing the original cue-outcome learning.
claims.temporal_ordering: Outcome omission occurs during extinction before later retrieval or return-of-fear testing.

causal_assumptions.consistency: The replication closely followed the critical original protocol.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Participants were assigned across reactivation and standard-extinction conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Between-group difference in later conditioned-response recovery for reactivation-extinction versus standard extinction.

confidence.rationale: A high-powered registered direct replication found no benefit, and reanalysis found weak support for the original between-group claim.

limitations: Null advantage in one protocol is not proof that memory updating is impossible.

boundary_conditions: This does not rule out every reconsolidation-based protocol or boundary condition.
scope.population: Healthy adults meeting conditioning and extinction inclusion criteria.
scope.temporal_scope: Reminder approximately ten minutes before extinction and recovery testing one day later.

claims.statement: Reactivation followed by extinction within ten minutes does not currently show a robust advantage over ordinary extinction for preventing later fear recovery in humans.
claims.temporal_ordering: Randomized reminder timing precedes extinction and delayed recovery testing.

evidence.design: Within-participant ABA renewal test in distinct virtual-reality contexts after short-delay extinction.

effect.metric: renewal contrast across acquisition and extinction test contexts
effect.notes: Renewal was observed in fear-potentiated startle, skin conductance, and fear ratings.

limitations: Exact standardized effects were not extracted in this pilot.
evidence.population: Healthy human volunteers completing differential aversive conditioning and extinction.
evidence.summary: Conditioned responding returned when testing moved from the extinction context, despite short-delay extinction.

evidence.design: Fully crossed context-shift and acquisition-to-extinction-delay experiment with next-day testing in the acquisition context.

effect.metric: context specificity of differential skin-conductance fear return
effect.notes: Fear return was more selective to CS+ in context-shift than same-context groups, F(1,61)=4.94, p=.03.

evidence.extraction_locator: Participants; Fear renewal test; Results, Figure 3.
limitations: Differential attrition and responder availability reduced some phase-specific samples.
evidence.population: Sixty-six recruited healthy young adults; complete-case counts varied by analysis.
evidence.summary: Returning to the acquisition context produced selective renewal relative to remaining in the extinction context.

evidence.design: Immediate versus 24-hour delayed extinction crossed with same versus shifted physical context.

effect.metric: main effect of acquisition-to-extinction interval on fear-relapse difference score
effect.notes: F(1,61)=6.93, p<.01; spontaneous recovery appeared after immediate but not delayed extinction, while delayed context-shift renewal was transient.

limitations: Timing manipulation changes more than one possible memory process.
evidence.population: Sixty-six recruited healthy young adults; complete-case counts varied by analysis.
evidence.summary: Delayed testing revealed return of responding, but its form depended on acquisition-to-extinction timing and physical context.

evidence.design: Standard cue-only extinction versus compound deepened extinction with 24-hour spontaneous-recovery test.

effect.notes: Deepened extinction reduced recovery of skin conductance and was associated with lower shock expectancy than standard extinction.

limitations: The study does not directly observe an inhibitory memory trace.
Exclusions based on acquisition and extinction performance can affect generalizability.
evidence.population: Healthy adult volunteers; 51 participants contributed to the reported expectancy comparison after exclusions.
evidence.summary: Changing the extinction procedure altered next-day return of responding, consistent with extinction being modifiable learning rather than mere fatigue.

evidence.design: High-powered preregistered direct replication of the critical reactivation-extinction conditions from Schiller et al. 2010 Experiment 1.

effect.metric: reactivation-extinction versus standard-extinction difference in fear recovery
effect.notes: The registered replication found no evidence that reactivation-extinction persistently attenuated fear recovery.

limitations: Results delimit this protocol and do not test every reconsolidation boundary condition.
evidence.population: Healthy adults in a three-day differential fear-conditioning experiment.
evidence.summary: The preregistered direct replication did not reproduce the claimed advantage of the ten-minute reactivation-extinction procedure.

metadata.description: Human experimental records separating extinction procedure, within-session response reduction, extinction-memory retrieval, and later return of fear. The pack treats inhibitory learning as an explanatory hypothesis rather than an observed synonym for response reduction.
metadata.title: Primary evidence pack for fear extinction and return of fear

objects.scope: Human laboratory tests; return of a measured response is not equivalent to clinical relapse.

boundary_notes: This integrative mechanism is compatible with several formal learning models.
